task.title: Find the goroutines internal/cli's command tests leave behind
task.description: Measured on feat/cli-test-speed (PR #153) while checking a go test -count=2 run of internal/cli: the second iteration cost 207 s against 127 s for a single run, and a goroutine census inside TestMain showed about 455 goroutines before the first iteration and about 1790 before the second, so roughly 1300 outlive the tests that started them. Only about 70 belong to the serve and watcher helpers; the rest is one to three per ordinary command test, which points at the product's command path rather than at test scaffolding. A long-lived workbook serve or the desktop's watcher runs commands in one process the same way, so this is worth aiming at the product first. Start from the census method in the branch's final-fix-2 report: count runtime.NumGoroutine before and after one command test, then use a goroutine profile to name the leaked stacks. Under a normal single run the leak costs nothing visible; it only matters for -count runs and long-lived processes.
